summary: Iteration 51 — Verified Email OTP rate-limit fix in services/email_otp.py:request_otp. 6/6 backend tests pass. Fix confirmed working end-to-end: count_documents now runs BEFORE update_many, and prior unused OTPs are marked superseded (used_at + superseded=true) instead of deleted, so they still count toward the 5/hour quota. TTL cleans them up after 10 minutes.
verified_behaviors: Sophia's 5 x POST /api/otp/request {purpose:'withdrawal'} → 200; 6th → 400 with body {detail:'Too many OTP requests. Try again in an hour.'}. Verified message contains 'Too many OTP requests' and 'hour'.

DB state after 5 successful requests: exactly 5 rows in email_otps for (user, purpose='withdrawal'), of which exactly 1 has used_at=None (the newest) and 4 have superseded=true. Newest row is not marked superseded.

verify_otp still works after supersede fix: fresh user + 1 x seller_apply → OTP row created with superseded!=true → brute-forced sha256 code from code_hash → POST /api/otp/verify → 200 with otp_token starting 'otp_' and expires_in_seconds=300.
Independent quotas per purpose: same fresh user, 5 x withdrawal all 200, 6th withdrawal 400, but 1 x seller_apply on that same user still returns 200.
Invalid purpose 'garbage' → 400 with detail containing 'Unknown purpose'.
Auth guard on /api/otp/request: no Authorization header → 401/403.
critical_code_review_comments: services/email_otp.py:59 — the raise still uses an unnecessary f-string ('f"Too many OTP requests..."' with no interpolation). Minor, from iter50 review, still not addressed.
routers/otp.py — get_db() is invoked directly rather than via Depends(get_db). Works, but inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's DI pattern. Carried over from iter50.

TTL of 10 min means superseded rows disappear after 10 min. Consequence: if a user requests 5 OTPs within a short window, waits ~10 minutes, then requests again, all 5 old rows may have TTL-expired and the quota effectively resets. This is a design choice, not a bug — the 1-hour window is a soft guarantee that only holds while rows are still within TTL. Consider extending TTL of superseded rows to 1h to make the hourly cap strict, OR keep a separate lightweight otp_request_log collection with 1h TTL for accurate counting.

email_otp.py: the update_many superseded marker uses the same used_at field as verify_otp's 'consumed' marker. Distinguishing consumed vs superseded is only via the 'superseded' boolean — fine, but a status enum would be clearer.
test_credentials: sophia_style@demo.local / demo1234; also registers fresh users e2e_otp_<ts>_<hex>@example.com / pass1234 via POST /api/auth/register
seed_data_creation: Test creates and cleans up its own email_otps rows via direct Mongo delete_many for sophia (withdrawal, seller_apply buckets) and for the fresh user (all purposes). Fresh user account itself is left in DB (harmless — unique timestamped email).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 50's bug (rate-limit bypass via delete_many-before-count) is FIXED and verified. The fix keeps superseded OTP rows in DB (used_at=now, superseded=true) so they still count toward the 5/hour window. When writing future OTP-related tests, remember Mongo TTL (10 min) will eventually clean up superseded rows, so use fresh unique test users to keep quota buckets deterministic. Existing test_iteration50_email_otp.py still covers the guarded-endpoint side (withdrawal + seller_apply guards, single-use otp_token, TTL indexes, cashout/password_reset purposes). This iteration_51 test file is the regression suite for the rate-limit fix specifically.
rca of the issue: Original bug (iter50): request_otp deleted prior unused OTPs BEFORE counting, so count_documents({created_at>=hour_ago}) always saw ≤1 row. Fix (verified this iter): (1) count_documents runs first (line 55-57 of email_otp.py); (2) update_many marks prior unused rows as used_at=now + superseded=true (lines 75-78) rather than delete_many; (3) insert_one(new row). Rate-limit trip verified at N=6. verify_otp continues to work because its query filters on used_at=None and expires_at>now, and the newest row (inserted AFTER update_many) has used_at=None so it's the only match. Superseded rows are correctly ignored by verify.
